readings.title: The Borders of the Land
readings.text: [Numbers 34:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Command the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land of Kena’an, this is the land that falls to you as an inheritance, the land of Kena’an by its boundaries:</dq> [3] <dq>‘And your southern border shall be from the Wilderness of Tsin along the border of Eḏom, and your southern boundary shall be from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And your boundary shall turn from the south to the Ascent of Aqraḇḇim, and pass over to Tsin, and its exit shall be to the south of Qaḏĕsh Barnĕa. And it shall go on to Ḥatsar Addar, and pass over to Atsmon.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And the boundary shall turn from Atsmon to the wadi of Mitsrayim, and its exit shall be at the Sea.</dq> [6] <dq>‘As for the western boundary, you shall have the Great Sea for a boundary. This is your western boundary.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And this is your northern boundary: From the Great Sea you shall mark out your boundary line to Mount Hor.</dq> [8] <dq>‘From Mount Hor you shall mark out your boundary to the entrance of Ḥamath, and the exit of the boundary shall be at Tseḏaḏ.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And the boundary shall go on to Ziphron, and its exit shall be at Ḥatsar Ěnan. This is your northern boundary.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall mark out your eastern boundary from Ḥatsar Ěnan to Shepham.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And the boundary shall go down from Shepham to Riḇlah on the east side of Ayin. And the boundary shall go down and reach to the eastern side of the Sea of Kinnereth.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And the boundary shall go down to the Yardĕn, and its exit shall be at the Salt Sea. This is your land according to its boundaries all around.’ ”</dq> [13] And Mosheh commanded the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “This is the land which you inherit by lot, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded to give to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe. [14] “For the tribe of the children of Re’uḇen according to the house of their fathers, and the tribe of the children of Gaḏ according to the house of their fathers, have received their inheritance. And half the tribe of Menashshĕh has received its inheritance. [15] “The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Yardĕn of Yeriḥo eastward, toward the sunrise.”

readings.title: The Appointed Apportioners
readings.text: [Numbers 34:16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [17] <dq>“These are the names of the men who divide the land among you as an inheritance: El’azar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun.</dq> [18] <dq>“And take one leader from every tribe to divide the land for the inheritance.</dq> [19] <dq>“And these are the names of the men: from the tribe of Yehuḏah, Kaleḇ son of Yephunneh;</dq> [20] <dq>“and from the tribe of the children of Shim’on, Shemu’ĕl son of Ammihuḏ;</dq> [21] <dq>“from the tribe of Binyamin, Eliḏaḏ son of Kislon;</dq> [22] <dq>“and a leader from the tribe of the children of Dan, Buqqi son of Yog̱li;</dq> [23] <dq>“from the children of Yoseph: a leader from the tribe of the children of Menashshĕh, Ḥanni’ĕl son of Ěphoḏ,</dq> [24] <dq>“and a leader from the tribe of the children of Ephrayim, Qemu’ĕl son of Shiphtan;</dq> [25] <dq>“and a leader from the tribe of the children of Zeḇulun, Elitsaphan son of Parnaḵ;</dq> [26] <dq>“and a leader from the tribe of the children of Yissaḵar, Palṭi’ĕl son of Azzan;</dq> [27] <dq>“and a leader from the tribe of the children of Ashĕr, Aḥihuḏ son of Shelomi;</dq> [28] <dq>“and a leader from the tribe of the children of Naphtali, Peḏah’ĕl son of Ammihuḏ.”</dq> [29] These were the ones whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded to divide the inheritance to the children of Yisra’ĕl in the land of Kena’an.

readings.title: Inheritance of the Lĕwites
readings.text: [Numbers 35:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh in the desert plains of Mo’aḇ by the Yardĕn of Yeriḥo, saying, [2] <dq>“Command the children of Yisra’ĕl that they shall give to the Lĕwites cities to dwell in from the inheritance of their possession, and also give to the Lĕwites open land around the cities.</dq> [3] <dq>“And the cities shall be theirs to dwell in, and their open land shall be for their livestock, and for their herds, and for all their beasts.</dq> [4] <dq>“And the open land of the cities which you give to the Lĕwites shall be from the wall of the city outward, a thousand cubits all around.</dq> [5] <dq>“And you shall measure outside the city on the east side two thousand cubits, and on the south side two thousand cubits, and on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits, with the city in the midst. This shall be to them the open land of the cities.</dq> [6] <dq>“And the cities which you give to the Lĕwites shall be the six cities of refuge, which you give for the manslayer to flee to, and to these you shall add forty-two cities.</dq> [7] <dq>“All the cities which you give to the Lĕwites shall be forty-eight cities, with their open land.</dq> [8] <dq>“And the cities which you give shall be from the possession of the children of Yisra’ĕl. From the larger tribe you take many, and from the smaller you take few. Each one gives some of its cities to the Lĕwites, according to the inheritance which it inherits.”</dq>

readings.title: Justice and the Cities of Refuge
readings.text: [Numbers 35:9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [10] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you pass over the Yardĕn into the land of Kena’an,</dq> [11] <dq>‘then you shall choose cities to be cities of refuge for you, that the manslayer who smites a being by mistake shall flee there.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And they shall be cities of refuge for you from the revenger, so that the manslayer does not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And of the cities which you give, let there be six cities of refuge for you.</dq> [14] <dq>‘Give three cities beyond the Yardĕn, and give three cities in the land of Kena’an, as cities of refuge.</dq> [15] <dq>‘These six cities shall be for refuge for the children of Yisra’ĕl, and for the stranger, and for the settler in their midst, for anyone who smites a being by mistake to flee there.</dq> [16] <dq>‘But if he has smitten him with an instrument of iron, so that he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And if he has smitten him with a stone in the hand, by which one could die, and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [18] <dq>‘Or if he has smitten him with a wooden instrument in the hand, by which one could die, and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [19] <dq>‘The revenger of blood himself shall put the murderer to death. When he meets him, he puts him to death.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And if he thrusts him through in hatred, or threw an object at him while lying in wait, so that he dies,</dq> [21] <dq>‘or in enmity he smote him with his hand, so that he dies, the one who smote him shall certainly be put to death, for he is a murderer. The revenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when he meets him.</dq> [22] <dq>‘But if he thrust him suddenly without enmity, or threw an object at him without lying in wait,</dq> [23] <dq>‘or used a stone, by which one could die, throwing it at him without seeing him, so that he dies, while he was not his enemy nor seeking his harm,</dq> [24] <dq>‘then the congregation shall judge between the smiter and the revenger of blood according to these right-rulings.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And the congregation shall deliver the manslayer from the hand of the revenger of blood, and the congregation shall return him to the city of refuge where he had fled, and he shall dwell in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the set-apart oil.</dq> [26] <dq>‘But if the manslayer at any time goes outside the boundary of the city of refuge where he had fled,</dq> [27] <dq>‘and the revenger of blood finds him outside the boundaries of his city of refuge, and the revenger of blood slays the manslayer, he is not guilty of blood,</dq> [28] <dq>‘because he should have dwelt in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. But after the death of the high priest the manslayer shall return to the land of his possession.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And these shall be a law of right-ruling for you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.</dq> [30] <dq>‘Whoever smites a being, the murderer shall be put to death by the mouth of witnesses, but one witness does not bear witness against a being to die.</dq> [31] <dq>‘And you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death, but he shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And you shall take no ransom for him who has fled to his city of refuge to return to dwell in the land before the death of the priest.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And do not profane the land where you are, for blood profanes the land. And the land is not pardoned for the blood that is shed on it, except by the blood of him who shed it.</dq> [34] <dq>‘And do not defile the land which you inhabit, in the midst of which <dn>I</dn> dwell, for <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, am dwelling in the midst of the children of Yisra’ĕl.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Guarding the Tribal Allotment
readings.text: [Numbers 36:1] And the heads of the fathers of the clans of the children of Gil’aḏ son of Maḵir, son of Menashshĕh, of the clans of the sons of Yoseph, came near and spoke before Mosheh and before the leaders, the heads of the fathers of the children of Yisra’ĕl, [2] and they said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded my master to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and my master was commanded by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to give the inheritance of our brother Tselopḥaḏ to his daughters. [3] “And if they are married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Yisra’ĕl, then their inheritance shall be taken from the inheritance of our fathers, and shall be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they marry. So it shall be taken from the lot of our inheritance. [4] “And when the Yoḇĕl of the children of Yisra’ĕl comes, then their inheritance shall be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they marry. So their inheritance shall be taken from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.” [5] And Mosheh commanded the children of Yisra’ĕl according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “What the tribe of the sons of Yoseph speaks is right. [6] “This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded for the daughters of Tselopḥaḏ, saying, <dq>‘Let them be married to whom they think best, but let them be married only within the clan of their father’s tribe.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And the inheritance of the children of Yisra’ĕl shall not change hands from tribe to tribe, for every one of the children of Yisra’ĕl shall cling to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Yisra’ĕl, shall be the wife of one of the clan of her father’s tribe, so that the children of Yisra’ĕl each possess the inheritance of his fathers.</dq> [9] <dq>‘Thus the inheritance shall not change hands from one tribe to another, but every tribe of the children of Yisra’ĕl shall cling to its own inheritance.’ ”</dq> [10] As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh, so did the daughters of Tselopḥaḏ. [11] For Maḥlah, Tirtsah, and Ḥog̱lah, and Milkah, and No’ah, the daughters of Tselopḥaḏ, were married to the sons of their father’s brothers. [12] They were married into the clans of the sons of Menashshĕh son of Yoseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of their father’s clan. [13] These are the commands and the right-rulings which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded by the hand of Mosheh to the children of Yisra’ĕl in the desert plains of Mo’aḇ by the Yardĕn of Yeriḥo.
